newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Belgacom Mobile close to U.S. roaming deal.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Belgacom Mobile close to U.S. roaming deal.

text.p: Belgian mobile phone company Belgacom Mobile SA said on Thursday it was in talks with five U.S. operators about setting up roaming deals in the United States, and was close to concluding an agreement with one.
"I signed something yesterday with one of them - we are awaiting their signature," Belgacom Mobile managing director Jan Neels told a news conference in answer to a question.
He decline to name any of the five.
"We're talking to several because the (mobile telephone) traffic is in different areas across the United States," Neels added.
Belgacom Mobile SA is 75-percent owned by Belgian state telephone company Belgacom, and 25-percent owned by U.S. AirTouch Communications. It runs Belgium's first GSM network, Proximus.

Rival Mobistar which runs Belgium's second GSM network, said last Friday it and four other GSM operators signed a deal with U.S. American Personal Communications (APC) to launch transatlantic roaming with the areas of Washington D.C. and Baltimore.
Mobistar is owned 62-percent by France Telecom, Belgian data communications company Telinfo has 10 percent and a group of eight other Belgian investors has 28 percent.

Belgacom Mobile, which has 440,000 customers, also announced on Thursday it was trying to attract new Proximus users by offering 15-day mobile phone trials with money-back guarantees. The offer ran from February 22 to March 31.

It was also offering customers the possibility to have one phone number for two SIM cards. This would mean they could make calls from two phones with just one subscription and without having to switch SIM cards between them.
Parent company Belgacom is 49-percent owned by a consortium including Ameritech, Singapore Telecom, Tele Danmark and three Belgian groups. The remaining 51 percent is owned by the Belgian state.
